item.title: OpenAI Sees $70B Revenue; Airtel Money Seeks Biggest UK IPO Since 2021
item.description:
Bloomberg Daybreak Europe is your essential morning viewing to stay ahead. Live from Brussels, we set the agenda for your day, catching you up with overnight markets news from the US and Asia. And we'll tell you what matters for investors in Europe, giving you insight before trading begins.
On today's show, global stocks edged higher following a tech-led selloff, while Brent oil slid after President Trump said the US won't attack Iran before the midterms.
Bloomberg understands OpenAI is expecting annualized revenue of at least $70 billion by the end of the year, scotching rumours it was set to miss some estimates.
And Airtel Money makes its debut on the London Stock Exchange in what's set to be the UK's biggest IPO in five years.
Today's guest: Adam Dunnett, European Union Chamber of Commerce in China, Secretary General. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Nobel Peace Prize Bets for Navalny’s Widow Surge on Polymarket
item.description: Bets for who will take home the 2026 Nobel Peace Prize surged overnight on Polymarket, echoing similar events a year ago when a website hacking likely leaked the winner’s name.
item.dc:creator: Ott Ummelas and Emily Nicolle

item.title: Why Ethiopia-Eritrea Tensions Pose Another Threat to Red Sea Shipping
item.description: Ethiopia is on a precipice, with rival armed forces mobilizing across the country, old alliances fracturing and clashes intensifying.
item.dc:creator: Simon Marks

item.title: Azadeh Moaveni Says Melania Trump Is Misunderstood
item.description: US journalist Azadeh Moaveni is best known for her coverage of Iran and the Middle East. She reflects on a seismic year at home and abroad, and why she wrote a book about the wives of US presidents. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: US Won't Attack Iran Before Midterms, Trump Says
item.description: US President Donald Trump said in a social media post on Thursday that the US would not be attacking Iran before November’s midterm elections. His decision comes despite Iran escalating attacks on tankers in the Strait of Hormuz, Tehran-backed militants in Yemen attacking energy facilities in Saudi Arabia and Trump’s decision to move US bombers from a base in the UK because of possible Iran-linked threats. Bloomberg's Stuart Livingstone-Wallace reports. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Russia’s ICC Chief Extradition Request Regrettable, Japan Says
item.description: A senior Japanese government spokesperson said it was regrettable that the Russian Prosecutor General’s Office had requested that Dutch authorities extradite International Criminal Court President Tomoko Akane and eight other officials.
item.dc:creator: Sakura Murakami

item.title: Anutin’s Key Ally Backs Thai Coalition Despite Flood Criticism
item.description: Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul’s key coalition partner is standing behind his government even as its handling of severe flooding draws criticism and risks eroding public confidence.
item.dc:creator: Suttinee Yuvejwattana and Anuchit Nguyen

item.title: Labour Defeats Greens to Hold Starmer’s Former London Seat
item.description: The UK’s Labour Party won a special election for a central London parliamentary seat early Friday morning, providing a boost to Prime Minister Andy Burnham and a blow to Green leader Zack Polanski.
item.dc:creator: Lucy White

item.title: New Delhi Deploys Heavy Security Ahead of Voter-Roll Protest
item.description: From mass detentions to liquor-store closures, authorities in New Delhi are leaving little to chance as they prepare for a weekend of protests over a contentious revision of India’s voter rolls.
item.dc:creator: Rajesh Roy

item.title: Insults Punctuate El-Sayed, Rogers Fiery Michigan Senate Debate
item.description: A debate Thursday night in the closely watched Michigan Senate race quickly turned acrimonious, with Democrat Abdul El-Sayed and former Republican congressman Mike Rogers trading insults, accusations and even comparisons about their mothers.
item.dc:creator: Jeff Green

item.title: US Moves to Reassure Taiwan as Trump-Xi Ties Stall Big Arms Deal
item.description: The US has allowed a flurry of engagements with Taiwan in the wake of Donald Trump’s lavish welcome for China’s Xi Jinping, signaling support for the island democracy even as it keeps a major arms sale in limbo ahead of more meetings between the leaders this year.
item.dc:creator: Yian Lee

item.title: Trump: US Won't Attack Iran Before Midterm Elections
item.description: "Balance of Power" focuses on the intersection of politics and global business. On today's show, Rep. Raja Krishnamoorthi (D-IL) says Iran could take advantage militarily and economically of President Trump's announcement that the US will not attack Iran before the midterm elections. Brett Bruen, President of the Global Situation Room and former US diplomat, says Iran may not go along with President Trump's effort to keep tensions down before the midterm elections and could continue using attacks to demonstrate its leverage. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: The Debrief with Mario Parker: Tight Race Republicans Confront Trump Dilemma
item.description: Bloomberg's Mario Parker joins to discuss Republican candidates distancing themselves from President Trump in key races and strategists' concerns about his approval rating for The Debrief. He speaks with Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Bruen: Political Power Is Diffusing in Post-American Era
item.description: Brett Bruen, President of the Global Situation Room and former US diplomat, says Iran may not go along with President Trump's effort to keep tensions down before the midterm elections and could continue using attacks to demonstrate its leverage. Bruen says President Trump cannot speak on behalf of Israel and says Netanyahu will make his own calculations based in part on his political prospects. Bruen says leaders in Europe, Canada, Japan and the Middle East are starting to build their own structures as political power diffuses in what he calls a "post-American era," creating a new economic and political dynamic. He speaks with Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Rep. Krishnamoorthi: This War Is a Disaster
item.description: Rep. Raja Krishnamoorthi (D-IL) says Iran could take advantage militarily and economically of President Trump's announcement that the US will not attack Iran before the midterm elections. Rep. Krishnamoorthi says he doesn't put much stock in President Trump's claim that the US is having productive discussions with Iran and says the conflict is benefiting China and Russia by drawing US forces and munitions toward the Middle East. He speaks with Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Mamdani Calls on Trump to End ICE Operations After NYC Shooting
item.description: Mayor Zohran Mamdani called for an end to federal immigration enforcement in New York City after an ICE officer shot and wounded a man in front of a child, escalating tensions over the Trump administration’s crackdown.
item.dc:creator: Myles Miller

item.title: US-Sanctioned Tycoon Becomes Zimbabwe’s Investment Minister
item.description: Zimbabwe’s President Emmerson Mnangagwa has appointed a tycoon sanctioned by the US and UK for alleged corruption as the country’s investment minister.
item.dc:creator: Ray Ndlovu, Antony Sguazzin and Godfrey Marawanyika

item.title: African Nations Ask Ukraine to Return Captured Prisoners
item.description: African nations are calling for Ukraine to return their citizens who are being held in its prisoner of war camps after they were caught fighting for Russia.
item.dc:creator: David Herbling, Antony Sguazzin and Volodymyr Verbianyi

item.title: Trump Says US Won’t Attack Iran Before Midterm Elections
item.description: President Donald Trump said in a social media post that the US would “not be attacking Iran” before November’s midterm elections, citing what he said were “productive discussions” with the Islamic Republic.
item.dc:creator: Jennifer A. Dlouhy and Ellen Milligan

item.title: US Bars Microsoft, Indian Firms From Visa Program in Blow
item.description: The Trump administration accused Microsoft Corp., Adobe Inc. and a half-dozen other companies of abusing a US worker visa program and suspended them indefinitely from a longstanding immigration initiative that’s served as a crucial talent pipeline for Silicon Valley and Wall Street.
item.dc:creator: Jennifer A. Dlouhy, Matt Day and Alicia A. Caldwell
